summary: Hisao Kanaseki was a scholar of Buddhist studies and other fields who studied at Doshisha University (~1938–1941). He held professorships at Kobe University (~1963–1974), Tokyo Metropolitan University (~1974–1982), and Komazawa University (~1982–1993).

Hisao Takahashi, an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar, studied at Taisho University (~1971–1976) and under Ryukai Mano. He spent his career at Taisho University as an assistant (~1974–1983), lecturer (attested 1995), and professor (~1996–2015).

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, Hisashi Matsumura studied under Jan Willem de Jong. He held posts at the Australian National University (attested 1982) and as associate professor at Kobe Shinwa Women's University (attested 1996–1997).

Hisashi Sato worked in Tibetology and history/archaeology, having studied at Kyoto University (~1934–1937). He served as a professor at Kyoto University (~1964–1977), Bukkyo University (~1977–1984), Toyo University, and Komazawa University.

Hisataka Ishida specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and completed his doctorate at the University of Vienna (-2011) under Helmut Krasser, later teaching at Aichi Gakuin University (attested 2015).

Philosopher Hisatake Kato studied at the University of Tokyo (~1957–1961). His academic posts included Yamagata University (~1971–1980), University of Tokyo (~1980–1989), Tohoku University (~1989–1996), and Tottori University of Environmental Studies (~2001–2007).

Hisayoshi Miyamoto works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy, having studied under Kamlesh Dutt Tripathi. He was a professor at Toyo University and serves as a lecturer at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

A scholar of Buddhist studies, Hitoshi Inui studied under Kanjin Horiuchi. He held academic positions at Koyasan University as a lecturer (attested 1986–1992) and later as a professor (attested 2015).

Hitoshi Kato is a scholar of Buddhist studies. In 1992, he was attested at Otani University, Osaka University of Foreign Studies, and Nara University of Education, later holding an attested post at Osaka University in 2016.

Hjalmar Frisk was a Swedish scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at the University of Gothenburg. He taught at Lund University (1937) and served as professor of comparative Indo-European and Sanskrit at Gothenburg (1938–1967).

Hla Pe was a linguist who studied at the University of Rangoon (~1934–1938) and the University of London (~1938–1944). He taught Burmese language and culture at SOAS from 1948 and served as Professor of Burmese (1966–1980).
Ho-chin Yang is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Yang studied at the University of Washington, completing a PhD in 1994 under the supervision of Leonard van der Kuijp.
Hogen Bays is a figure in Buddhist and religious studies who studied under traditional teacher Shodo Harada. Bays has served as co-abbot at the Great Vow Zen Monastery.
Hoin Yamada is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied at Ryukoku University (~1959–1963) and was a student of Gyōin Hashimoto.
Hoju is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Peking University (~1999–2003) and KU Leuven (~2005–2007), and taught Kyokuga Saeki.

Hoju Shioda is a Buddhist studies scholar who holds posts as deputy director and assistant professor at Minobusan University (attested 2026), and has also lectured at Doho University and Daido University.

Hojun Nagasaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara. He was a professor at Otani University (~1970–1999) and president of the Japan Association of Jain Studies (1998).
Hokai was a scholar in the field of Buddhist studies who studied under Hogetsu and Zuihe.
Hokei Izumi was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Otani University under Bunyiu Nanjio. He later served as a professor at Otani University (attested 1930).
Hoko Kuwana is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (attested 2015) and holds a post as director at Minobusan University (attested 2026).
